mainTopic: Which items are subject to פיגול (only things with a מתיר), and עולא's ruling that a פיגול קומץ loses its פיגול status on the מזבח
overview: The amud opens by finishing a list from the משנה of things that are not subject to פיגול, and the arguments about libations and the מצורע's oil. The basic rule is that פיגול only applies to something that has a מתיר, another part of the offering (usually the blood) that makes it permitted. The משנה gives examples of how blood permits different offerings. רבי שמעון limits פיגול to offerings whose blood goes on the outer altar, like שלמים. The גמרא then brings עולא, who says a פיגול קומץ loses its פיגול status once it is brought onto the מזבח. The גמרא explains his reasoning and then asks what new law he is teaching, trying three possibilities that a משנה already covers. It answers that עולא means a קומץ the fire already caught, which is put back up if it falls off. Finally the גמרא points out that עולא already said this rule elsewhere, and the answer to that challenge comes on the next amud.

steps.title: More items on the list that are not subject to פיגול
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues its list of things that are not subject to פיגול: מנחת כהנים, the מנחה of the כהן משיח, the blood, and libations brought on their own. This is the view of רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Also the meal offering of כהנים, the meal offering of the anointed כהן, the blood, and libations that are brought by themselves are not subject to פיגול. This is what רבי מאיר says.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is finishing a list it started just before this point. The list names things for which a person is not punished with כרת for פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item on this list has nothing else that permits it. A מנחת כהנים is burned completely, with no קומץ to permit it. The blood is itself the thing that permits the offering. Since פיגול only applies to something that gets permitted by another part, these items are left out.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering made invalid because the כהן intended to eat or burn it after its proper time; eating it carries כרת
A meal offering brought by a כהן, burned completely on the altar
The anointed כהן גדול
Libations of wine (and the accompanying flour-and-oil offering)
By themselves, as a separate offering

steps.confusionAlert: This is the middle of a list. The words 'these are things for which one is not liable for פיגול' came just before this point, so every item here is not subject to פיגול.

phrases.english: and the meal offering of priests,
and the meal offering of the anointed priest,
and the blood, and the libations
that are brought by themselves.
These are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of items exempt from פיגול that began just before this point
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מנחת כהנים, the מנחה of the כהן משיח, the blood, and libations brought on their own are not subject to פיגול (רבי מאיר).

steps.title: The Sages include libations that come with an animal
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say that even libations that come together with an animal offering are not subject to פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: even libations that come along with an animal offering are not subject to פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים disagree with רבי מאיר about libations. They say the exemption from פיגול also covers libations that come with an animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר only exempted libations brought on their own. That suggests he holds that libations which come with an animal are tied to the animal's blood and can become פיגול. The חכמים hold that libations are never made permitted by the animal's blood, so they are never subject to פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority opinion
Those that come with an animal offering

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
Even those that come with the animal.
phrases.notes: He means libations, which are also not subject to פיגול.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אַף הַבָּאִין עִם הַבְּהֵמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes רבי מאיר's limit on libations
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Libations are never subject to פיגול, even when they come with an animal offering.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: the מצורע's oil is not subject to פיגול
steps.stepSummary: About the לוג of oil brought by a מצורע, רבי שמעון says one is not liable for פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: The לוג of oil of a מצורע: רבי שמעון says one is not liable for it because of פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a new case, the oil that a healed מצורע brings. רבי שמעון says it is not subject to פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון treats the oil as something that is not permitted by anything else. Without a מתיר, the איסור of פיגול does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: A liquid measure, a little more than a quarter liter
A person who had צרעת and brings offerings when he is healed
One is not liable

phrases.english: The log of oil of a leper —
Rabbi Shimon says:
One is not liable for it due to piggul,

steps.triggerLanguage: לוֹג שֶׁמֶן שֶׁל מְצוֹרָע – רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new case: the מצורע's oil
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, the מצורע's לוג of oil is not subject to פיגול.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: the oil is subject to פיגול because the אשם's blood permits it
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says the oil is subject to פיגול, because the blood of the מצורע's אשם is what permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says one is liable for it because of פיגול, since the blood of the אשם permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר disagrees with רבי שמעון and gives his reason. The oil does have a מתיר: the blood of the אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The oil can only be used after the אשם's blood has been put on the מצורע. Since the blood makes the oil usable, the oil has a מתיר. That means it can become פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: Guilt offering; here, the one the מצורע brings
Permits it, makes it usable
One is liable

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir says:
One is liable for it due to piggul;
since the blood of the guilt offering permits it,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: חַיָּיבִין עָלָיו מִשּׁוּם פִּיגּוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes רבי שמעון about the oil
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מצורע's oil is subject to פיגול, because the אשם's blood permits it.

steps.title: The general rule: anything with a מתיר is subject to פיגול
steps.stepSummary: Anything that has a מתיר, whether it permits the item to a person or to the altar, is subject to פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Anything that has things that permit it, whether for a person or for the altar, one is liable for it because of פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה states the main rule behind this whole topic. If something becomes permitted through another part of the offering, it can become פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This rule explains the whole list. It does not matter whether the מתיר lets a person eat the item or lets it go on the altar. Either way, פיגול applies. Things with no מתיר, or things that are themselves the מתיר, are not included.

keyTerms.meaning: Permitting factors, the parts of an offering (usually the blood) that make other parts permitted
Whether for a person or for the altar

steps.whatToRemember: פיגול only applies to something that has a מתיר. This explains why the blood, the libations, and a completely burned מנחה are left out.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle is the key used across the סוגיא to decide which items are subject to פיגול.

phrases.english: and anything that has permitting factors
whether for a person or for the altar —
one is liable for it due to piggul.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ מַתִּירִין בֵּין לָאָדָם בֵּין לַמִּזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the general principle that supports רבי מאיר's reasoning and explains the whole list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anything that has a מתיר, for a person or for the altar, is subject to פיגול.

steps.title: Examples of how blood permits different offerings
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives examples. The עולה's blood permits its flesh for the altar and its hide for the כהנים. The bird עולה's blood permits its flesh for the altar. The bird חטאת's blood permits its meat for the כהנים. The blood of the burned bulls and goats permits their אימורים to go on the altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: The עולה: its blood permits its flesh for the altar and its hide for the כהנים. The bird עולה: its blood permits its flesh for the altar. The bird חטאת: its blood permits its meat for the כהנים. Burned bulls and burned goats: their blood permits their אימורים to be offered.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains what it means for something to have a מתיר by listing several offerings. In each one, the blood permits something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These examples show both kinds of permitting from the rule: for a person (hide or meat for the כהנים) and for the altar (flesh or אימורים burned). So each of these offerings can become פיגול. The last example, the burned bulls and goats, sets up רבי שמעון's argument in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Burnt offering, burned completely on the altar
A bird burnt offering
A bird sin offering, eaten by the כהנים
Bulls that are burned outside the camp, whose blood is brought inside
The fats and parts of an offering that are burned on the altar

phrases.english: The burnt offering — its blood permits
its flesh for the altar
and its hide for the priests.
The bird burnt offering — its blood permits
its flesh for the altar.
The bird sin offering — its blood permits
its meat for the priests.
Bulls that are burned and goats that are burned —
their blood permits their sacrificial portions to be offered.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָעוֹלָה – דָּמָהּ מַתִּיר אֶת בְּשָׂרָהּ לַמִּזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives examples of the general rule about מתירין
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In each of these offerings the blood is the מתיר, so they are subject to פיגול.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: only offerings on the outer altar, like שלמים, are subject to פיגול
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says that any offering whose blood is not placed on the outer altar, the way שלמים are, is not subject to פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: anything that is not on the outer altar like שלמים, one is not liable for it because of פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון disagrees with the last example. He limits פיגול to offerings that are done on the outer altar, like שלמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה taught פיגול about שלמים, whose blood goes on the outer altar. רבי שמעון says פיגול only applies to offerings that are like שלמים in this way. So the burned bulls and goats, whose blood is brought inside, are not subject to פיגול even though their blood permits their אימורים.

keyTerms.meaning: The outer altar, in the courtyard
Peace offerings; the offering about which the תורה teaches פיגול

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון, having a מתיר is not enough. The offering must also be done on the outer altar, like שלמים.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
Anything that is not on the outer altar
like peace offerings,
phrases.notes: He means its blood is not placed on the outer altar, the way it is with שלמים.

phrases.english: one is not liable for it due to piggul.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: כֹּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ עַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ הַחִיצוֹן כִּשְׁלָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues with the example of the burned bulls and goats
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Offerings whose blood is not placed on the outer altar like שלמים are not subject to פיגול.

steps.title: עולא: a פיגול handful loses its פיגול status on the altar
steps.stepSummary: עולא rules that a קומץ that is פיגול, once brought up on the מזבח, loses its פיגול status. He supports this with a קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: עולא said: A handful that is פיגול that was brought up onto the altar has lost its פיגול status. If it brings other things to פיגול, all the more so itself!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with a new statement from עולא about a קומץ that is פיגול. He says that once it is placed on the מזבח, it is no longer treated as פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קומץ is the part that makes the rest of the מנחה פיגול. עולא reasons with a קל וחומר: if the קומץ has the power to affect other things, then surely it is affected itself. How that reasoning gets him to 'its פיגול left it' is not yet clear, and the next step asks about it.

keyTerms.meaning: The handful of flour taken from a מנחה and burned on the מזבח
An offering ruined by a wrong intention about the time it will be eaten or burned
Fell away, left; here, the status is gone
All the more so (a קל וחומר)

phrases.english: GEMARA: Ulla said:

phrases.aramaic: קוֹמֶץ פִּיגּוּל שֶׁהֶעֱלוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ –
phrases.english: A handful that is piggul that one brought up onto the altar,
its piggul status has left it;
if it brings others to piggul,
phrases.notes: The 'others' are the rest of the מנחה, the part the כהנים eat.

phrases.english: is it itself not all the more so?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא on the משנה about items that are subject to פיגול.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קומץ that is פיגול, once brought onto the מזבח, loses its פיגול status.

steps.title: What does עולא mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how עולא's 'all the more so' reasoning proves that the פיגול status leaves the קומץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what עולא's reasoning means. This short question sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As it stands, the קל וחומר seems to prove the opposite. If the קומץ makes others פיגול, you would expect it to be פיגול itself, not to lose that status. So the גמרא asks for clarification.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he saying? (asking for the meaning of a statement)

phrases.english: What is he saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reasoning of עולא's statement in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the קל וחומר supports the claim that the פיגול status leaves the קומץ.

steps.title: The קומץ must be 'accepted' to make others פיגול
steps.stepSummary: עולא means: if the קומץ were not counted as accepted on the מזבח, it could not make the rest of the מנחה פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he is saying: If it is not accepted, how can it bring others to פיגול?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains עולא's reasoning. A קומץ only makes the rest of the מנחה פיגול when it is offered in a way that counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מנחה only becomes פיגול if its קומץ is otherwise offered properly ('accepted'). Since the קומץ does make the rest פיגול, its offering must count as accepted. So once it is on the מזבח, it is treated as properly offered and no longer counts as פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means
Accepted; the offering counts as properly brought

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
If it is not accepted,
how can it bring others to piggul?

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The קומץ's offering must count as accepted, or else it could not make the rest of the מנחה פיגול. So on the מזבח it is no longer treated as פיגול.

steps.title: Not about liability, since a משנה already says that
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what עולא adds. If he means there is no כרת for eating the קומץ, a משנה already lists the קומץ as something with no פיגול liability.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us? If it is that one is not liable for it because of פיגול, we already learned: These are things one is not liable for because of פיגול: the handful, the incense, the frankincense, the מנחה of כהנים, the מנחה of the כהן משיח, the מנחה of נסכים, and the blood!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges עולא: what new law is he teaching? It tries a first guess and shows that a משנה already teaches it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liability for פיגול applies to things permitted by a מתיר, not to the מתיר itself. The קומץ is a מתיר, so the משנה already says nobody is liable for eating it, whether or not it went up on the מזבח. So עולא cannot be teaching that.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us (that is new)?
Incense
Frankincense placed with a מנחה
The anointed כהן גדול

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?

phrases.aramaic: אִי דְּאֵין חַיָּיבִין עָלָיו מִשּׁוּם פִּיגּוּל –
phrases.english: If it is that one is not liable for it because of piggul,
we already learned it:

phrases.aramaic: אֵלּוּ דְּבָרִים שֶׁאֵין חַיָּיבִין עֲלֵיהֶם מִשּׁוּם פִּיגּוּל:
phrases.english: These are the things one is not liable for because of piggul:
the handful, the incense, and the frankincense,
and the meal offering of priests, the meal offering of the anointed priest,
the meal offering of libations, and the blood!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that עולא's reasoning is clear, the גמרא asks what practical law he adds.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that עולא's point is that one is not liable for eating the קומץ.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה already says the קומץ never brings liability for פיגול, so this would teach nothing new.

steps.title: Not 'if they went up they don't come down', since a משנה already says that
steps.stepSummary: Second guess: עולא teaches that a פיגול קומץ, once on the מזבח, is not taken down. But a משנה already says this about פיגול and other disqualified items.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, that if they went up they do not come down. We already learned: What was left overnight, what went out, what is impure, and what was slaughtered with intent outside its time or outside its place: if they went up, they do not come down!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second meaning of עולא's statement and again shows it is already in a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists items with a פסול that are left on the מזבח if they already got there. One of them is an offering slaughtered with intent 'outside its time,' which is פיגול. So the rule for a פיגול קומץ on the מזבח is already known.

keyTerms.meaning: If they went up (on the מזבח), they are not taken down
Left overnight past its time
Taken out of its allowed area
Intent for outside its time, which makes it פיגול

phrases.english: Rather, that if they went up they do not come down,
we already learned:
What was left overnight, what went out, and what is impure,
and what was slaughtered with intent outside its time or outside its place:
if they went up, they do not come down!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second explanation of what עולא teaches after the first was rejected.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that עולא teaches that a פיגול קומץ on the מזבח is not removed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה already rules that disqualified items, including פיגול, stay on the מזבח once they got there.

steps.title: Not 'if they came down they go back up', since the משנה says the opposite
steps.stepSummary: Third guess: עולא teaches that a פיגול קומץ that fell off the מזבח is put back. But the same משנה says items that came down are not put back up.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, that if they came down they go back up. This too we already learned: Just as if they went up they do not come down, so if they came down they do not go back up!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a third meaning, and shows that a משנה rules the opposite way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the suggestion is that because the קומץ lost its פיגול status, it should be put back if it fell off. But the משנה says disqualified items that came down are not returned. So this explanation contradicts a משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: If they came down, they go back up
This too we already learned

phrases.english: Rather, that if they came down they go back up,
this too we already learned:
Just as if they went up they do not come down,
so if they came down they do not go back up!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a third explanation after the second was rejected.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that עולא teaches that a פיגול קומץ that came down is put back up.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה explicitly says disqualified items that came down are not put back up.

steps.title: עולא means a case where the fire already caught
steps.stepSummary: עולא's ruling is needed for a case where the fire had already taken hold of the קומץ before it fell. Then it is put back on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed where the fire has taken hold of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that עולא is speaking about a special case: the קומץ had already started burning on the מזבח and then fell off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's rule 'if they came down they do not go back up' covers items that came down before the fire took hold. Once the fire caught the פיגול קומץ, its פיגול status is gone, so עולא teaches that it is returned to the מזבח. This is the new point עולא adds.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for (a specific case)
The fire has taken hold of them

steps.whatToRemember: עולא: a פיגול קומץ loses its פיגול status on the מזבח. In practice, if the fire already caught it and it fell off, it is put back up. The משנה's rule that items which came down are not put back up applies only before the fire caught them.
steps.confusionAlert: עולא does not disagree with the משנה. The משנה's 'if they came down they don't go back up' covers items the fire had not caught yet. עולא is speaking only about a קומץ the fire already caught.

phrases.english: No, it is needed
where the fire has taken hold of them.
phrases.notes: The קומץ had already started burning and then fell off, so עולא says it goes back up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13 by limiting עולא to a special case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: עולא seemed to repeat or contradict known משניות.
steps.terutzMaskana: עולא speaks about a קומץ the fire already caught. Since its פיגול status left it, it is returned to the מזבח if it falls.

steps.title: Didn't עולא already teach this rule somewhere else?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 14. עולא already stated, as a general rule, that items the fire took hold of are put back on the מזבח. So this ruling about the קומץ seems to repeat something he already said.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this too עולא already said on another occasion. עולא said: The משנה taught that items that came down are not put back up only when the fire had not taken hold of them. But if the fire had taken hold of them, they are put back up!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. It points out that עולא already taught this exact rule in a general way, so the case of the קומץ would add nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 14 the גמרא said עולא's ruling teaches that a קומץ the fire had grabbed is put back on the מזבח. Here the גמרא brings a different statement of עולא: the משנה's rule that fallen items are not put back applies only when the fire had not taken hold of them. Since that general statement already covers this case, the קומץ ruling looks like a repeat. The גמרא answers what is new on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: One time, meaning on another occasion. He already said it once.
They only taught this when... It narrows the משנה to a specific case.
The fire took hold of them. The fire had already started burning the item.
They should go up, meaning they are put back on the מזבח.

steps.confusionAlert: This line does not argue with the הלכה itself. The גמרא accepts that, according to עולא, an item the fire took hold of is put back up. The only question is why עולא would need to say the rule twice.

phrases.english: But this too, עולא already said it
phrases.notes: "This" is the answer from Step 14: a קומץ the fire took hold of is put back on the מזבח.

as עולא says:

phrases.notes: He means the משנה from Step 13 that says items that came down from the מזבח are not put back up.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא נָמֵי אַמְרַהּ עוּלָּא חֲדָא זִימְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of Step 14 by showing that עולא already taught the same rule in a general statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 14 that עולא's ruling about the קומץ is needed for a case where the fire already took hold of it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Repetition: עולא already said in general that the משנה's rule (items that came down are not put back) applies only when the fire had not taken hold. So putting back a burning item is already known, and the קומץ ruling would teach nothing new.
